draft.title: Kepler's laws
card: First law
Each planet moves in an ellipse, with the Sun at one focus. An ellipse is a stretched circle, and a circle is a special case.
Second law
A line from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times. So a planet moves faster when it is closer to the Sun and slower when it is further away.
Third law
For bodies orbiting the same central mass, r³/T² is the same constant. Here r is the orbital radius (the average distance for an ellipse) and T is the orbital period.
So a larger orbit has a longer period. If two bodies orbit the same mass, r₁³/T₁² = r₂³/T₂².
draft.remember: Ellipses, equal areas in equal times, and r³/T² constant for one central mass.

a.q: A comet orbits the Sun in an ellipse. Where in its orbit is the comet moving fastest?
opts: At its closest point to the Sun
At its furthest point from the Sun
At the midpoint of its path, at the average distance
It moves at the same speed everywhere
a.why: The line to the Sun sweeps equal areas in equal times. Near the Sun the line is short, so the comet must cover more distance along its path to sweep the same area. Constant speed would only suit a circular orbit, and the first law says orbits are ellipses.
a.clue: A short line to the Sun must cover more path to sweep the same area.

b.q: Moon A orbits a planet at a radius of 4.0 × 10⁵ km with a period of 2.0 days. Moon B orbits the same planet at a radius of 1.6 × 10⁶ km. What is the period of Moon B?
opts: 16 days
8.0 days
4.0 days
32 days
b.why: Both moons orbit the same planet, so r³/T² is equal. The radius is 4 times larger, so r³ is 64 times larger. T² is 64 times larger, so T is 8 times larger: 16 days. Choosing 8.0 days wrongly treats T as proportional to r³.
b.clue: Find how many times larger r³ is, then take the square root for T.

a.best: At its closest point to the Sun

problems.detail: The why says choosing 8.0 days 'wrongly treats T as proportional to r³'. That is false. Treating T as proportional to r gives 4 × 2.0 = 8.0 days. Treating T as proportional to r³ would give 64 × 2.0 = 128 days. The distractor explanation misdiagnoses the error and should say it treats T as proportional to r.

check.summary: Both questions are correct (closest point; 16 days), but the why for question b misexplains the 8.0-day distractor: it comes from treating T as proportional to r, not r³.
